DIS.rationale: Disney delivered a clear beat-and-raise Q2 (fiscal 2026) with revenue of $25.17B (+6.5% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.57 beating consensus by 5.4%, driven by broad-based growth across Experiences (+7%), Entertainment (+10%), and Sports (+1%). The new CEO Josh D'Amaro's first earnings season showed strong execution: streaming operating income surged 88% YoY, parks revenue grew 7% with higher guest spending, and management raised full-year adjusted EPS growth guidance to ~12% (from 'double digits'). Capital returns accelerated with the buyback target raised to $8B and share count reduced 2.3% YoY. Balance sheet remains solid with $115B equity and a debt-to-equity ratio of ~0.43-0.48, providing financial flexibility. Valuation at 15.6x P/E sits in the lower half of its 12.5-23.8x 12-month range, and P/B of 1.67 is near the bottom of its 1.5-2.1x range, suggesting the market is not fully pricing in the improving trajectory. The Q2 report and guidance raise represent a credible near-term re-rating catalyst that has already begun (stock surged ~7-8% post-earnings). However, several headwinds temper conviction: (1) GAAP EPS declined 29.8% YoY due to one-time items, (2) the FCC's unprecedented early license review of ABC stations creates regulatory overhang, (3) rising oil prices ($98/bbl) could pressure park attendance and consumer spending, and (4) 10-year Treasury yields at 4.41% and rising create a headwind for growth multiples. The score reflects solid fundamentals with improving trajectory and reasonable valuation, partially offset by regulatory and macro risks.

Disney streaming, theme parks drive revenue in first earnings report under CEO Josh D'Amaro. Disney reported $25.17 billion in quarterly revenue on Wednesday, beating Wall Street expectations. Operating income exceeded the company's prior guidance.

Disney's entertainment segment – which includes its traditional TV, streaming and theatrical releases – saw revenue increase 10% to $11.72 billion compared with the same period last year. Subscription and affiliate fees climbed 14% to $7.8 billion, boosted by recent streaming price hikes.
The FCC has ordered Disney's ABC to file early license renewals for eight major TV stations by May 28, citing possible violations of anti-discrimination rules.

Former CEO Bob Iger's $42M insider selling contrasts with new CEO's equity awards, signaling internal division. Institutional investors reduced Disney holdings, while Experiences segment generates 71.9% of profits as a financial buffer.
